what_it_does: This paper describes a temperature sensor chip made from bipolar junction transistors (BJTs—specialized transistor types used for analog circuits). Temperature sensors need to measure heat with high precision while using very little power. The researchers use a technique called a continuous-time delta-sigma modulator, which is a way to convert analog signals (like voltage changes caused by temperature) into digital numbers. They add a clever current-balancing amplifier to make the measurement more sensitive while keeping noise low. The result is a sensor that uses only 80 femtojoules per measurement per Kelvin squared—an energy efficiency metric—which is much better than older resistor-based approaches.
